translations.idiomatic: Shidao's female kin were spared harsh confiscation.

sentences.zh: 以宣歙觀察使竇易直為潤州刺史，充浙西觀察使韓弘進助平淄青絹二十萬匹，女樂十人。

translations.literal: Xuan-She observation commissioner Dou Yizhi was made Run prefect; Western Zhe observation commissioner Han Hong presented two hundred thousand bolts of silk to aid pacifying Ziqing and ten female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yizhi went to Run; Han Hong sent silk and entertainers for Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 女樂還之。

translations.literal: The female musicians were returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the musicians back.

sentences.zh: 六月丁未朔。

translations.literal: Sixth month, dingwei new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth month opened on dingwei.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以福建觀察使元錫為宣州刺史、宣歙池觀察使。

translations.literal: guichou — Fujian observation commissioner Yuan Xi was made Xuan prefect and Xuan-She-Pool observer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xi took Xuan-She on guichou.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以戶部侍郎歸登為工部尚書。

translations.literal: gengshen — Revenue Vice Minister Gui Deng was made Works Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Deng became works minister on gengshen.

sentences.zh: 以鄭州刺史裴乂為福州刺史、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: Zheng Prefect Pei Yi was made Fuzhou prefect and Fujian observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi took Fujian.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，敕定州大都督府復上州。

translations.literal: xinyou — an edict: Dingzhou metropolitan prefecture again became a superior prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou was restored to upper-prefecture rank on xinyou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以前兵部尚書李絳檢校吏部尚書、河中尹，充河中晉張慈隰觀察使。

translations.literal: jiazi — former War Minister Li Jiang was made acting Personnel Minister, Hezhong Intendant, and Hezhong-Jin-Zhang-Ci-Sui observer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang took Hezhong on jiazi.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔左金吾大將軍胡證充京西北巡邊使，所經鎮戍，與守將審量利害，具事實奏聞。

translations.literal: guiyou — an edict: Left Golden Guard Grand General Hu Zheng shall be capital northwest frontier inspection commissioner; at each garrison and post, with defending generals weigh benefit and harm, set out facts, and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zheng was sent to inspect northwest defenses on guiyou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁丑。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, dingchou.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh month reached dingchou.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，汴州韓弘來朝。

translations.literal: wuyin — Bianzhou's Han Hong came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong presented himself at court on wuyin.

sentences.zh: 己卯，左散騎常侍致仕薛蘋卒。

translations.literal: jimao — Left Regular Cavalry Attendant in retirement Xue Pin died.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Pin died on jimao.

sentences.zh: 乙酉夜，月掩心大星。

translations.literal: yiyou night — the moon covered the great Heart star.
translations.idiomatic: The moon occulted Antares on yiyou night.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，群臣上尊號曰元和聖文神武法天應道皇帝。

translations.literal: xinsi — the hundred officials offered the honorific title "Sacred, Cultured, Divine, Martial, Law-Aligning, Heaven-Responding Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed a grand honorific on xinsi.

sentences.zh: 是日，御宣政殿受冊，禮畢，御丹鳳樓，大赦天下。

translations.literal: That day — at Xuanzheng Hall he received the investiture; when rites ended, he ascended Danfeng Tower and proclaimed a great amnesty for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He took the title and amnestied the empire the same day.

sentences.zh: 京畿今年秋稅、青苗、榷酒等錢，每貫量放四百文；

translations.literal: This year's capital-region autumn tax, green-sprout, and monopoly wine cash — for each string four hundred cash were remitted;
translations.idiomatic: Capital taxes were cut four hundred cash per string;

sentences.zh: 元和五年已前逋租賦並放。

translations.literal: arrears in rent and tax before Yuanhe 5 were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: and pre-Yuanhe 5 arrears were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 甲午，韓弘進糸也絹二十八萬匹，銀器二百七十事。

translations.literal: jiawu — Han Hong presented two hundred eighty thousand bolts of silk and two hundred seventy silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong gave lavish gifts on jiawu.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以河陽三城懷州節度使、朝議郎、使持節懷州諸軍事、守懷州刺史、兼御史大夫、賜紫金魚袋令狐楚可朝議大夫、過中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: dingyou — Heyang Three Cities Huai military commissioner, Court Discussion Doctor, holder of the staff for Huai military affairs, Huai prefect, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, granted gold-purple fish bag Linghu Chu was made Court Discussion Doctor, concurrent Chancellery Vice Director and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu entered the council on dingyou.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以永州刺史韋正武為邕管經略使。

translations.literal: renyin — Yong prefect Wei Zhengwu was made Yongguan disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhengwu took Yongguan on renyin.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以前黔中觀察使魏義通為懷州刺史、河陽三城懷孟節度使。

translations.literal: guimao — former Qianzhong observation commissioner Wei Yitong was made Huai prefect and Heyang Three Cities Huai-Meng military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yitong took Heyang on guimao.

sentences.zh: 沂州軍亂，殺節度使王遂。

translations.literal: Yi prefecture army mutinied and killed military commissioner Wang Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui was killed in the Yi mutiny.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以棣州刺史曹華為沂州刺史，充沂、海、兗密等州都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: jiachen — Di Prefect Cao Hua was made Yi prefect and observer over Yi, Hai, Yan, and Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hua was sent to crush Yi on jiachen.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，罷晉州防禦使。

translations.literal: yisi — Jinzhou defense commissioner was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou defense was abolished on yisi.

sentences.zh: 八月丁未朔。

translations.literal: Eighth month, dingwei new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth month opened on dingwei.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，制宣武軍節度副大使、知節度事、汴宋亳潁等州觀察處置等使、開府儀同三司、守司徒、兼侍中、汴州刺史、上柱國、許國公、食邑三千戶韓弘可守司徒、兼中書令，宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: yiyou — by decree, Xuanwu military vice commissioner in charge, observer over Bian, Song, Bo, Ying, and disposition, Palace Equal in Honor with the Three Excellencies, acting Master of Works, concurrent Palace Attendant, Bian prefect, Upper Pillar, Duke of Xu with three thousand households Han Hong could keep acting Master of Works, concurrent Secretariat Director, and Xuanwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong was made Secretariat director on yiyou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，於襄州穀城縣置臨漢監以牧馬，仍令山南東道節度使兼充監牧使。

translations.literal: jiayin — at Xiangzhou Gucheng county Linhan Pasturage was established to raise horses; the Shannan East military commissioner was ordered to hold it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: A Linhan stud was set under Shannan East on jiayin.

sentences.zh: 戊午，王承宗進位檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: wuwu — Wang Chengzong was promoted to acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong received an honorary vice-directorship on wuwu.

sentences.zh: 己未，田弘正來朝。

translations.literal: jiwei — Tian Hongzheng came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng arrived at court on jiwei.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「天下事重，一日不可曠廢。

translations.literal: The Emperor told the councillors: "Empire affairs are weighty — one day cannot be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said state business could not wait even on holidays.

sentences.zh: 若遇連假不坐，有事即詣延英請對。

translations.literal: If consecutive holidays come and we do not sit, when there is business go to Yanying to present it."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered ministers to seek audience at Yanying whenever needed."

sentences.zh: 」崔群以殘暑方甚，目同列將退。

translations.literal: Cui Qun, because brutal heat was extreme, looked as if his colleagues would withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun tried to leave in the heat.

sentences.zh: 上止之曰：「數日一見卿等，時雖暑熱，朕不為勞。

translations.literal: The Emperor stopped them: "Several days pass before I see you — though it is hot, I am not troubled."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong kept the council despite summer heat.

sentences.zh: 」久之方罷。

translations.literal: Only after long time were they dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The audience ran long.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，宴田弘正與大將判官二百人於麟德殿，賜物有差。

translations.literal: dinghai — Tian Hongzheng and two hundred generals and staff were feasted at Linde Hall; gifts were graded.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng's officers were feasted on dinghai.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，陳許節度使、檢校刑部尚書郗士美卒。

translations.literal: wuchen — Chen-Xu military commissioner, acting Penal Minister Heshimei died.
translations.idiomatic: Heshimei died on wuchen.

sentences.zh: 九月丙子朔。

translations.literal: Ninth month, bingzi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth month opened on bingzi.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，考功郎中蕭祐進古畫、古書二十卷。

translations.literal: wuyin — Merit Examination Bureau Director Xiao You presented twenty scrolls of ancient paintings and books.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao You offered antiquities on wuyin.

sentences.zh: 斬沂州亂首王弁於東市。

translations.literal: The Yi mutiny ringleader Wang Bian was beheaded at the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bian was executed for the Yi revolt.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以國子祭酒李遜檢校禮部尚書、許州刺史、忠武軍節度、陳許溵蔡等觀察使。

translations.literal: guiwei — National University Chancellor Li Xun was made acting Rites Minister, Xu prefect, Zhongwu military commissioner, and Chen-Xu-Yin-Cai observer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun took Zhongwu on guiwei.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，貶右衛大將軍田縉為衡王傅。

translations.literal: gengyin — Right Guard Grand General Tian Ji was demoted to Prince of Heng staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji was demoted on gengyin.

sentences.zh: 縉前鎮夏州，私用軍糧四萬石，強取黨項羊馬，致黨項引吐蕃入寇故也。

translations.literal: Ji had formerly commanded Xiazhou, privately used forty thousand shi of army grain, forcibly took Dangxiang sheep and horses, causing Dangxiang to bring Tibet to raid — hence demotion.
translations.idiomatic: He had provoked Tibet by plundering Dangxiang.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以太子少師鄭餘慶兼判國子祭酒。

translations.literal: jiawu — Crown Prince Junior Tutor Zheng Yuqing was made concurrent National University Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing took the university on jiawu.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以田弘正兄相州刺史田融檢校刑部尚書，兼太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: xinchou — Tian Hongzheng's elder brother Xiang Prefect Tian Rong was made acting Penal Minister, concurrent Crown Prince Guest, and eastern-capital absentee.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong was honored in Luoyang on xinchou.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以魏博節度使、光祿大夫、檢校司徒、同平章事、兼魏州大都督長史、上柱國、沂國公、食邑三午戶田弘正依前檢校司徒、兼侍中，賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: jiachen — Weibo military commissioner, Grand Mentor of the Palace, acting Master of Works, Grand Councillor, concurrent Wei metropolitan senior administrator, Upper Pillar, Duke of Yi with three thousand households Tian Hongzheng kept acting Master of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant, granted three hundred households of real fief.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng received a real fief on jiachen.

sentences.zh: 時弘正三上表乞留闕庭，不許。

translations.literal: At the time Hongzheng thrice memorialized begging to remain at court — not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He had asked to stay in Chang'an three times in vain.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，上顧謂宰臣曰：「朕讀《玄宗實錄》，見開元初銳意求理，至十六年已後，稍似懈倦，開元未又不及中年，何也？

translations.literal: yisi — the Emperor looked at the councillors and said: "I read the Veritable Record of Emperor Xuanzong and saw that in the early Kaiyuan he was keen to seek good government, but from the sixteenth year afterward he seemed somewhat slack and weary; by late Kaiyuan he did not equal the middle years — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong asked why Xuanzong's reign faded after Kaiyuan 16.

sentences.zh: 」崔群對曰：「玄宗少歷民間，身經迍難，故即位之初，知人疾苦，躬勤庶政。

translations.literal: Cui Qun replied: "Xuanzong in youth passed among the people and personally met hardship — hence when he first ascended he knew the people's suffering and personally labored at the myriad administrations.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun said early Xuanzong knew common hardship,

sentences.zh: 加之姚崇、宋璟、蘇頲、盧懷慎等守正之輔，孜孜獻納，故致治平。

translations.literal: Moreover Yao Chong, Song Jing, Su Ting, and Lu Huaiqian and other upright assistants diligently offered counsel — hence order and peace.
translations.idiomatic: and great ministers kept him honest until order returned.

sentences.zh: 及後承平日久，安於逸樂，漸遠端士，而近小人。

translations.literal: Later, long peace made him secure in pleasure and ease; he gradually kept distant from upright scholars and drew near petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Comfort then drew him to flatterers,

sentences.zh: 宇文融以聚斂媚上心，李林甫以奸邪惑上意，加之以國忠，故及於亂。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong pleased his heart by revenue extraction; Li Linfu confused his will with treachery; Guo Zhongyu was added — hence disorder.
translations.idiomatic: until Rong, Linfu, and Guozhong brought ruin.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以開元初為法，以天寶未為戒，即社稷無疆之福也。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty take early Kaiyuan as law and late Tianbao as warning — then the altars' blessing will be without limit."
translations.idiomatic: He urged Xianzong to imitate early Kaiyuan, not late Tianbao."

sentences.zh: 」時皇甫鎛以諂刻欺蔽在相位，故群因奏以諷之。

translations.literal: At the time Huangfu Bo with fawning harshness deceived in the council — hence Qun's memorial used this to admonish indirectly.
translations.idiomatic: The speech targeted Huangfu Bo on the council.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙午朔。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, bingwu new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth month opened on bingwu.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，安南軍亂，殺都護李象古並家屬，部曲千餘人皆遇害。

translations.literal: renxu — Annan army mutinied, killed Protector-General Li Xianggu and his household; over a thousand subordinates were all harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Annan troops massacred Li Xianggu's house on renxu.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以唐州刺史桂仲武為安南都護，潮州刺史韓愈為袁州刺史。

translations.literal: bingyin — Tang Prefect Gui Zhongwu was made Annan Protector-General; Chaozhou Prefect Han Yu was made Yuan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Zhongwu took Annan; Han Yu was moved nearer court.

sentences.zh: 是月，吐蕃寇鹽州。

translations.literal: That month Tibet raided Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet raided Yan that month.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙亥朔，以戶部尚書李鄘為太子賓客、東都留守。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, yihai new moon — Revenue Minister Li Yong was made Crown Prince Guest and Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong became Luoyang regent on yihai.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，靈武大將史敬奉破吐蕃於鹽州城下，賜敬奉實封五十戶賞之。

translations.literal: xinmao — Lingwu Grand General Shi Jingfeng broke Tibet below Yan prefecture's wall; Jingfeng was granted fifty households of real fief as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingfeng beat Tibet at Yan and was rewarded on xinmao.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以原王傅鄭權為右金吾大將軍，充右街使。

translations.literal: dingyou — Prince of Yuan staff officer Zheng Quan was made Right Golden Guard Grand General and right-street commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Quan took the right capital street on dingyou.

sentences.zh: 上服方士柳泌金丹藥，起居舍人裴濆上表切諫，以「金石含酷烈之性，加燒煉則火毒難制。

translations.literal: The Emperor took the alchemist Liu Bi's gold elixir medicine; Daily Recorder Pei Pei memorialized strongly remonstrating that "metal and stone contain fierce nature; with smelting, fire poison is hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Pei warned against Liu Bi's elixir,

sentences.zh: 若金丹已成，且令方士自服一年，觀其效用，則進御可也。

translations.literal: If the gold elixir is already complete, first order the alchemist to take it himself for one year and observe the effect — then present it to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: and asked the alchemist to test it for a year first."

sentences.zh: 」上怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was enraged.

sentences.zh: 己亥，貶裴濆為江陵令。

translations.literal: jihai — Pei Pei was demoted to Jiangling magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Pei was exiled to Jiangling on jihai.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙巳朔。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, yisi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth month opened on yisi.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，國子祭酒鄭餘慶奏見任文官一品至九品，外使兼京正員官者，每月於所請秋錢每貫抽十文，修國子監，從之。

translations.literal: gengxu — National University Chancellor Zheng Yuqing memorialized: current civil officials from first to ninth rank, and outer envoys with concurrent capital regular posts, each month from requested autumn cash ten cash per string were to be drawn to repair the National University — approved.
translations.idiomatic: A levy on officials would fund the university.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以諫議大夫、守中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事、上柱國、賜紫金魚袋崔群為潭州刺史、兼御史大夫，充湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: yimao — Remonstrating Doctor, acting Chancellery Vice Director, Grand Councillor, Upper Pillar, granted gold-purple fish bag Cui Qun was made Tan prefect and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun was sent to Hunan on yimao.

sentences.zh: 為皇甫鎛所譖。

translations.literal: He was slandered by Huangfu Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo had engineered his fall.

sentences.zh: 及群被貶，人皆切齒於鎛。

translations.literal: When Qun was demoted, people gnashed teeth at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The capital hated Huangfu Bo for it.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年十五年春正月甲戌朔，上以餌金丹小不豫，罷元會。

translations.literal: Yuanhe 15 — spring, first month, jiaxu new moon: because the Emperor had taken gold elixir and was slightly unwell, the New Year audience was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe 15 opened without New Year rites because of elixir sickness.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，鎮冀觀察使王承宗奏鎮冀深等州，每州請置錄事參軍一員，判司三員，每縣請置令一員，從之。

translations.literal: gengchen — Zhen-Ji observation commissioner Wang Chengzong memorialized that in Zhen, Ji, and Shen prefectures each prefecture should have one recording adjutant and three judge officers, and each county one magistrate — approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong won more civil posts in his circuit on gengchen.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以前湖南觀察使崔倰權知戶部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: renwu — former Hunan observation commissioner Cui Qun was made acting Revenue Vice Minister and acting revenue commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun returned to fiscal office on renwu.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，沂、海四州觀察使府移置於兗州，改觀察使曹華為兗州刺常陰晦，微雨雪，夜則晴明，凡十七日方霽。

translations.literal: bingxu — the Yi-Hai four-prefecture observation office was moved to Yanzhou; observation commissioner Cao Hua was made Yanzhou prefect; from spring first month onward it was constantly overcast, with light rain and snow, clearing at night — seventeen days before it cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hua moved the Yi-Hai command to Yanzhou amid seventeen days of gloomy weather.

sentences.zh: 丙申，月犯心大星，光彩相及。

translations.literal: bingchen — the moon trespassed the great Heart star, their light touching.
translations.idiomatic: The moon brushed Antares on bingchen.

sentences.zh: 廢齊州豐齊縣入長清，廢全節縣入歷城，廢亭山縣入章丘縣。

translations.literal: Qi prefecture's Fengqi county was abolished into Changqing; Quanjie county into Licheng; Tingshan county into Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Three Qi counties were merged away.

sentences.zh: 義成軍節度使劉悟來朝。

translations.literal: Yicheng military commissioner Liu Wu came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，上對悟於麟德殿。

translations.literal: wuxu — the Emperor received Wu at Linde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong met Liu Wu at Linde on wuxu.

sentences.zh: 上自服藥不佳，數不視朝，人情恟懼，及悟出道上語，京城稍安。

translations.literal: Since taking medicine the Emperor had been unwell and often did not hold court — popular feeling was fearful; when Wu went out and spoke on the road, the capital gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu's appearance eased panic while the emperor stayed ill.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以少府監韓璀為鄜州刺史、鄜坊丹延節度使。

translations.literal: gengzi — Palace Crafts Director Han Cui was made Yan prefect and Yan-Fang-Dan-Yan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Han Cui took Yan-Fang on gengzi.

sentences.zh: 是夕，上崩於大明宮之中和殿，享年四十三。

translations.literal: That evening the Emperor died at Zhonghe Hall in Daming Palace, age forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong died at forty-three that night in Daming Palace.

sentences.zh: 時以暴崩，皆言內官陳弘志弒逆，史氏諱而不書。

translations.literal: Because the death was sudden, all said the inner eunuch Chen Hongzhi murdered him — the historians avoided writing it.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor blamed eunuch Chen Hongzhi for regicide; annalists kept silent.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，宣遺詔。

translations.literal: xinchou — the testamentary edict was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The death edict was read on xinchou.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，移仗西內。

translations.literal: renyin — the imperial guard shifted to the western inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The guard moved west on renyin.

sentences.zh: 五月丁酉，群臣上謚曰聖神章武孝皇帝，廟號憲宗。

translations.literal: Fifth month, dingyou — the hundred officials offered the posthumous title Sacred, Divine, Accomplished in Culture and War, Filial Emperor; temple name Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he received temple name Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬於景陵。

translations.literal: gengshen — he was buried at Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Jingling on gengshen.

sentences.zh: 史臣蔣系曰：憲宗嗣位之初，讀列聖實錄，見貞觀、開元故事，竦慕不能釋卷，顧謂丞相曰：「太宗之創業如此，玄宗之致理如此，既覽國史，乃知萬倍不如先聖。

translations.literal: Historian Jiang Xi said: When Xianzong first succeeded, he read the veritable records of successive sages and, startled and admiring, could not put the scrolls down; he turned to the Chancellor and said: "Taizong's founding was like this, Xuanzong's ordering the realm was like this — having viewed the national histories, I know I am ten thousandfold inferior to the former sages.
translations.idiomatic: Historian Jiang Xi wrote that young Xianzong devoured Tang exemplars and confessed his inferiority to Taizong and Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 當先聖之代，猶須宰執臣僚同心輔助，豈朕今日獨為理哉！

translations.literal: In the former sages' age, still needing chancellors and ministers to assist with one heart — how could I today alone govern?"
translations.idiomatic: He knew even sage kings needed loyal ministers, not solo rule."

sentences.zh: 」自是延英議政，晝漏率下五六刻方退。

translations.literal: From then at Yanying he discussed government; the day clepsydra usually fell five or six notches before he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He held long Yanying sessions until late afternoon.

sentences.zh: 自貞元十年已後，朝廷威福日削，方鎮權重。

translations.literal: From Zhenyuan 10 afterward, court authority daily shrank and regional commissioners grew weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhenyuan 10 the throne had lost power to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 德宗不委政宰相，人間細務，多自臨決，奸佞之臣，如裴延齡輩數人，得以錢穀數術進，宰相備位而已。

translations.literal: Dezong did not entrust administration to chancellors; petty affairs among the people he often decided himself; treacherous men like Pei Yanling and several others advanced by revenue arithmetic — chancellors merely filled posts.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong bypassed chancellors for fiscal cronies like Pei Yanling.

sentences.zh: 及上自籓邸監國，以至臨御，訖於元和，軍國樞機，盡歸之於宰相。

translations.literal: When the Emperor from the princely residence supervised the state through accession, until Yuanhe, military and state pivots all returned to the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong restored civil rule to the council after decades of eunuch and fiscal sway.

sentences.zh: 由是中外咸理，紀律再張，果能剪削亂階，誅除群盜。

translations.literal: Hence inside and outside were all ordered, discipline was raised again, and he truly could cut down rebellious steps and execute the bandit hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Order returned and he crushed the great rebellions.

sentences.zh: 睿謀英斷，近古罕儔，唐室中興，章武而已。

translations.literal: Wise counsel and heroic decisiveness — in recent antiquity rarely matched; Tang's mid revival was Zhangwu alone.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xi ranked his strategic genius among Tang's rarest restorers.

sentences.zh: 任異、鎛之聚斂，逐群、度於籓方，政道國經，未至衰紊。

translations.literal: Pity that he employed Yi and Bo's revenue extraction and drove Qun and Du to the provinces — state principle did not yet reach decay and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fiscal hardliners and exiling Pei Du and Cui Qun marred the late reign.

sentences.zh: 惜乎服食過當，閹豎竊發，茍天假之年，庶幾於理矣！

translations.literal: Alas that he overdosed on elixir; eunuchs stole the moment — had Heaven granted more years, he might nearly have reached good order!
translations.idiomatic: Had he lived longer and avoided elixirs and eunuch murder, fuller order might have followed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：貞元失馭，群盜箕踞。

translations.literal: Appraisal says: Zhenyuan lost the reins; bandits squatted like winnowing baskets.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy opens: after Zhenyuan, rebels held the realm.

sentences.zh: 章武赫斯，削平嘯聚。

translations.literal: Zhangwu was majestic; he leveled the roaring gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong's majesty crushed their uprising.

sentences.zh: 我有宰衡，耀德觀兵。

translations.literal: We had chancellors; they displayed virtue and reviewed arms.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers paired virtue with force.

sentences.zh: 元和之政，聞於頌聲。

translations.literal: Yuanhe's government was heard in songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe rule lived on in praise.
